prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1323; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the left rear quarter panel of the claimant's vehicle. Both drivers reported to be stopped at the scene with vehicles drivable. Photos requested from both parties and a scene diagram obtained from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck and lower back stiffness and a sharp pain in the lower back when turning the torso. Claimant states they are not represented by an attorney and prefers to handle the claim directly. Advised claimant of the medical evaluation options and asked for the name of their treating provider, if any.

Entry 3: Claimant confirmed a visit to an urgent care clinic the day after the collision. Diagnosis noted as a lumbar strain with prescribed rest and anti-inflammatory medication. Requested the clinic records and signed authorization forms from the claimant. Claimant indicated a follow-up visit is scheduled.

Entry 4: Reviewed the insured's statement, which describes moving into the adjacent lane without seeing the claimant's vehicle in the blind spot. Insured accepts that a lane change without adequate checking was the likely cause. Liability appears clear on the insured side, pending the scene photos and the other party's account. Vehicle damage estimate requested from the repair facility.

Entry 5: Claimant returned the authorization forms and provided the clinic records. Records confirm the lumbar strain diagnosis and a note to return if symptoms persist. Claimant reports improvement but ongoing discomfort with prolonged sitting. Claim remains open pending the repair estimate, the follow-up medical report, and a decision on the injury evaluation.
